roadmap.summary: You already have direct frontend experience (4-month Frontend Engineering Internship at Marblewood Health) plus React, TypeScript and Jest listed — most core skills for a Junior Frontend Engineer are present; you mainly need portfolio proof, deployment/CI, and interview practice.

phases.title: Portfolio-grade React + TypeScript project (deployed, tested, accessible)
phases.description: Ship two small, production-like pieces: a small component library (3–5 components) + a demo feature page that uses them. Add tests, accessibility improvements, CI that runs tests, and a deployed link (Vercel) so you have a single URL to include on applications and your resume.

items: Decide scope: pick 3–5 reusable UI components (e.g., Button, Input, Modal/Dialog, Toast) and one demo feature page (e.g., simple settings form or small dashboard) that shows them wired to state and API stubs.

Create a GitHub repo, initialize with TypeScript + React (Vite or Next.js), add README stub with one-paragraph project description that calls out Marblewood Health internship and the feature you built.
Set up developer tooling: ESLint + TypeScript config, Prettier, simple commit hooks (Husky), and Storybook basic config for the components.
Create a minimal project board (To Do / In Progress / Done) and split tasks into issues for each component, test, story, and deployment step.

weeks.focus: Build components with typed APIs and tests
items: Implement 3 core components with strong TypeScript props and small internal docs/comments (Button, Input, Modal). Keep components accessible (aria, keyboard focus).

Write unit + interaction tests using Jest + React Testing Library for each component (focus on behavior: click, keyboard, form input). Target passing tests locally and create a baseline coverage badge.
Create Storybook stories for each component showing variants (sizes, disabled, error states) and a compositional story showing them together in the demo page.
Commit small, focused PR-style branches per component to practice clear commit messages and PR descriptions.
Build the demo feature page wiring components to local state and a tiny mocked API (fetch with a small Node/Express or mocked fetch). Ensure TypeScript types for API responses.
Run Lighthouse and axe accessibility checks on the demo page; fix the top 3 accessible/performance issues (e.g., correct alt text, reduce bundle by lazy-loading modal, use React.memo where helpful).
Set up GitHub Actions to run tests and storybook build on pushes; configure Vercel deployment (or Netlify) to auto-deploy main branch and add deployment URL to README.

Finalize README: 2–3 bullet technical summary, link to deployed demo, highlight that you owned the frontend feature at Marblewood Health and list key tools (React, TypeScript, Jest, Storybook, Vercel).

phases.title: Simulated on-the-job tasks and mock frontend interviews
phases.description: Do timed, realistic frontend tasks (bug fix + feature) and 1:1 mock interviews that mirror junior frontend screening: live React+TS coding, PR creation, and behavioral questions tied to internship experience.

weeks.focus: Timed take-home simulation and PR practice
items: Perform a 3-hour timed take-home task: implement one additional small component or a new feature on your demo app, include tests, and create a PR with a proper description and changeset.
Seed a small bug in your code (e.g., failing test or an accessibility issue), then fix it under a 60–90 minute timer and push a follow-up commit describing the fix in PR comments.
Record or write the PR description template you'll reuse in applications (what changed, why, testing notes, deployment link) and add a short checklist for reviewers.

weeks.focus: Mock interviews: technical, behavioral, and debugging
items: Schedule and complete 2 mock interviews (one technical live-coding in React+TS — component rendering/state/props — and one behavioral using STAR that emphasizes Marblewood Health internship ownership). Use a friend, mentor, or platforms like Pramp/Interviewing.io if available.
Do a 45–60 minute debugging session: receive a failing build or test (create one in your repo) and debug while verbalizing steps. Time it to 60–90 minutes to simulate on-the-job troubleshooting.
Solve 2 frontend-focused algorithm problems (LeetCode Easy) and one DOM/array pair problem under 30–45 minutes to stay sharp for screening phone screens.

phases.title: Targeted applications and networking (Austin, TX)
phases.description: Apply broadly but targeted: 6–10 high-quality applications that include your deployed link, tailored resume bullets referencing internship impact, and targeted outreach to engineers and recruiters in Austin.

weeks.focus: Apply and follow up — 8+ strong applications and outreach
items: Apply to at least 8 Junior Frontend Engineer / New Grad positions in Austin (use LinkedIn Easy Apply, Built In Austin, Indeed, Hired, AngelList for startups, and direct company career pages).

For each application: include the deployed demo link in the resume and application, a one-sentence callout in the cover/email referencing your Marblewood Health internship and the specific component/feature you shipped, and attach a short tailored resume bullet.

Send 10 personalized LinkedIn messages to frontend engineers or hiring managers at target companies: ask for 15-minute informational chats, include your deployed link, and note shared Austin/startup interest.
Track every application in a spreadsheet (company, role, date, applied via, link, referral contact) and prepare a templated follow-up message for hiring managers to use 7–10 days after applying.
